newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds underperform, focus on currency, rates.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds underperform, focus on currency, rates.

text.p: The Irish government bond market underperformed core Europe as concerns about Irish pound weakness versus sterling and interest rate concerns in the U.S. weighed on sentiment, dealers said.

"We have underperformed Europe," Riada economist Padhraic Garvey said. "Against bunds we have underperformed by two to three basis points so the respective spreads are out to 91 basis points in the 10-year from 89 and to 164 in the five-year from 161 basis points."

Although agreement on a Stability Pact by EU heads of state in Dublin last Friday was expected to stimulate convergence trade, there was not much evidence of new foreign buying interest in the market, Garvey said.
He said there was an initial knee-jerk reaction following the Friday announcement but trade remained thin.
"The Friday move was basically prices being marked up but there was very little dealt in those prices," Garvey said. "On Monday we did see some buying but it fell away on Tuesday and today," he said.

Garvey said two factors which dampened activity were firstly the weakness of the punt versus sterling and concerns about a rate hike in the U.S. after stronger-than-expected U.S. housing starts on Tuesday.
By 1711 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2006 was five pence lower at 108.35 to yield 6.79 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2001 was off two pence at 101.27, yielding 6.18 percent.
